question.problem: Find the surface area of the portion of the surface $z=2y+{x}^{2}$ whose projection onto the $xy$-plane is bounded by $y=8x,$ $x=1,$ and the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ defined by $z=f(x,y)$ with $(x,y)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

In this case, our surface is given by

$$
z=2y+{x}^{2},\,(x,y)\in D
$$

where the region $D$ is given by

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 8x},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14119930/assets/d2ca6ee66367bd86cd56fe3a4891dbd4b64d9e23d5b4d97c9650b3af184b423f.png)

Now, since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂z}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2y+{x}^{2})=2x, \\ \frac{∂z}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2y+{x}^{2})=2,\end{aligned}
$$

the surface area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+(2x)^{2}+(2)^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{5+4{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{8x}\sqrt{5+4{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{5+4{x}^{2}}\cdot y\,{|}_{0}^{8x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}8x\sqrt{5+4{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting $u=5+4{x}^{2},$ we get $\text{d}u=8x\,\text{d}x.$ Also, the limits must be changed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & 0 & 1 \\ u & 5 & 9\end{aligned}
$$

 

Substituting these into our integral, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}8x\sqrt{5+4{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{5}^{9}{u}^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{u}^{3/2}\,{|}_{5}^{9} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}({9}^{3/2}-{5}^{3/2}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(27-5\sqrt{5}).\end{aligned}
$$
